name: Sentinel-Code Security Core Seed Benchmark
description: Small deterministic seed set with deliberately vulnerable and safe code fixtures. Use as a regression baseline, not as a representative measure of real-world security coverage.

matching.lines: candidate and expected line ranges must overlap

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: Untrusted email is concatenated into a SQL statement.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: Authenticated route uses a caller-controlled user identifier without proving ownership.

cases.label: safe
cases.description: Invoice ownership is bound to the authenticated principal.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: Untrusted filename is concatenated into a shell command.

files.src/convert.py:
import subprocess
name = request.args["name"]
subprocess.run("convert " + name, shell=True, check=True)

cases.label: safe
cases.description: Executable and arguments are passed separately without a shell.

files.src/convert.py:
import subprocess
name = validate_image_name(request.args["name"])
subprocess.run(["convert", name], shell=False, check=True)

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: A request-controlled URL is fetched without destination validation.

cases.label: safe
cases.description: URL is validated against public HTTPS destinations and redirects are disabled.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: Request-controlled content is written to an HTML parsing sink.

cases.label: safe
cases.description: Request-controlled content is assigned as text rather than parsed HTML.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: A caller-controlled path segment is joined to a storage root and opened without containment validation.

cases.label: safe
cases.description: Resolved path is checked to remain beneath the storage root before it is served.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: XML is parsed without disabling external entity and DTD processing.

cases.label: safe
cases.description: DOCTYPE and external entities are disabled before parsing untrusted XML.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: MD5 is used as a password hash.

cases.label: safe
cases.description: Password hashing uses a password-oriented KDF with a unique salt.

files.src/auth.py:
import hashlib
digest = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", password.encode(), salt, 600000)
